title: Reminder Proof
user: Independent dental and outpatient clinics that need reliable appointment reminders, delivery proof, and fallbacks without replacing their EMR.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A dental-clinic software builder spent weeks on WhatsApp appointment reminders, was rejected repeatedly in verification, then had the account banned after three template messages without a useful appeal path.
OpenEMR’s reminder runner can fail when no reminders are due and has recurring-event and status-update problems, showing that reminder delivery must be observable rather than assumed.
A customer could select an apparently free appointment slot but received a no-available-users error, demonstrating the operational cost of opaque calendar synchronization failures.

recurrence: Three separate scheduling/reminder failure modes in 2025–26—provider account loss, reminder runner faults, and calendar mismatch—can directly create no-shows and staff callbacks.
current_workaround: Staff manually text/call patients, rely on one channel such as WhatsApp, or troubleshoot inside an EMR/calendar after a complaint.
incumbents_and_gap: OpenEMR, Cal.com, NexHealth, and reminder vendors own scheduling or messaging. Smaller clinics lack a vendor-neutral delivery ledger that retries across approved channels and makes failures actionable to front desk staff.
smallest_useful_product: EMR/calendar connector, consent-aware template sender, SMS/email/approved WhatsApp fallback policy, delivery/response timeline, and staff exception queue. Non-goals: clinical notes, diagnosis, full scheduling, or unapproved bulk messaging.
success_measure: A clinic records delivery or a staff-owned exception for 99% of scheduled reminder attempts and reduces reminder-related no-shows by 15% within 90 days.
monetization: subscription — $79/location/month plus messaging pass-through fits a recurring appointment volume and measurable no-show cost.
constraints: HIPAA/UK GDPR as applicable, patient consent/opt-out, minimal PHI, BAA/DPA readiness, jurisdictional SMS rules, and no medical advice.
why_distinct: It is a reliability and proof layer around an existing calendar/EMR, not another clinical management suite.
